`inspect.getsource()` failure is not evidence that serving predictions are incorrect. CPython resolves a class through `sys.modules[cls.__module__]` and its module’s `__file__`; missing registration can produce a misleading “built-in class” TypeError. Python’s documented dynamic-import recipe registers `sys.modules[spec.name] = module` before `spec.loader.exec_module(module)`. This repairs module discovery when source is available, but numerical parity requires a separate test. [CPython implementation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/3.11/Lib/inspect.py), [importlib recipe](https://docs.python.org/3/library/importlib.html#importing-a-source-file-directly).

Recommended repair: expose an explicit `build_model(config)` factory shared by training and the embedded predictor writer. Save architecture configuration, vocabulary size, padding/mask IDs, sequence length and positional conventions alongside one category model’s `state_dict`. Reconstruct through the factory, load with `strict=True`, and run both original and reloaded models in evaluation mode under `torch.inference_mode()`. This avoids source introspection as a checkpoint dependency. PyTorch recommends reconstructing the architecture and loading its state dictionary; `eval()` disables training-time dropout behavior. [PyTorch checkpoint guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/basics/saveloadrun_tutorial.html).

Proposed parity tests: compare candidate logits from the trained model, factory reload and generated predictor on identical short, maximum-length, overlength/truncated and mixed-length batched histories. Reserve space for the appended mask before left-padding; preserve identical truncation, position IDs and padding masks. Read the appended mask at the final nonpadding position—never `count-1`. Check finite scores, tolerance-based equality and singleton-versus-batch agreement. These tests establish parity for covered inputs; introspection success alone cannot. BERT4Rec’s original inference procedure appends a mask and predicts its item. [BERT4Rec paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690).
